name: Microsoft Entra ID

verdict.topBlocker: Unverified publisher status blocking user consent in target customer tenants.
verdict.summary: App registration in Microsoft Entra ID is instant and self-serve for initial development and testing. To allow end users across external organizations to consent without warnings, developers must complete Publisher Verification using a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account.

steps.title: Create App Registration in Microsoft Entra ID
steps.detail: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center, navigate to Identity > Applications > App registrations, and register a new application. Select whether the app will support single-tenant users, multitenant organizational accounts, or personal Microsoft accounts.

steps.title: Configure Platform Redirect URIs
steps.detail: Add redirect URIs on the Authentication page for Web, Single-page, or Desktop/Mobile platforms. URIs must use HTTPS (except localhost) and match exact character casing.

steps.title: Generate Client Credentials
steps.detail: Under Certificates & secrets, create a new client secret or upload a certificate for confidential client applications. Record the secret value immediately as it is not shown again.

steps.title: Configure Delegated Scopes & App Roles
steps.detail: Define the delegated permissions (such as User.Read or Mail.Read) and standard OIDC scopes like offline_access in your application manifest or API permissions tab.

steps.title: Execute OAuth 2.0 Auth Code & Token Requests
steps.detail: Test the login flow by constructing requests to the /authorize endpoint, receiving authorization codes, and exchanging them at the /token endpoint for access and refresh tokens.

steps.title: Test Account Consent & Admin Consent Flow
steps.detail: Sign in with test work/school or personal accounts to test user consent screens. If testing admin-restricted permissions, execute administrative consent flows.

steps.title: Setup Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program Account
steps.detail: Obtain a Partner One ID for a valid Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (CPP) Partner Global Account and verify that your domain matches the publisher domain.

steps.title: Partner Center Identity Verification
steps.detail: Wait for Microsoft Partner Center to verify your organization's legal identity and partner global account status.

steps.title: Link Partner ID for Verified Publisher Badge
steps.detail: In the Entra admin center app registration Branding & properties section, associate the verified MPN/PartnerID to remove risk warnings and receive the blue verified badge on consent screens.

requirements.note: A Microsoft Entra ID tenant and a work/school or personal Microsoft account are required to register applications in the Entra admin center.
Publisher domain must be configured on the app registration and must match the domain verified under the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account.
A verified Partner One ID from a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program partner global account is required for publisher verification.

scopes.note: Standard delegated permission to read the signed-in user's profile.
Delegated permission to read user mail; subject to user or admin consent depending on tenant policies.
Standard OIDC scope requested to obtain a refresh token for long-lived access.
Admin-restricted scope requiring Global Administrator consent in target organizational tenants.

blockers.symptom: User receives a warning screen that the app is unverified and risky, or is blocked from granting consent.
blockers.cause: The multitenant application is not Publisher Verified, and risk-based step-up consent policies in the user's tenant block consent.
blockers.unblock: Complete Publisher Verification by associating a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account with the app registration.

blockers.symptom: Error AADSTS50011: The reply URL specified in the request does not match the reply URLs configured for the application.
blockers.cause: The redirect URI sent in the authentication request does not match any redirect URI registered in the Entra admin center.
blockers.unblock: Ensure exact scheme, host, port, and path case matching when configuring redirect URIs in Authentication settings.

blockers.symptom: User is shown an error stating they are not authorized to consent to the requested permissions.
blockers.cause: The application requested high-privilege or admin-restricted permissions such as Directory.ReadWrite.All.
blockers.unblock: Request a Global Administrator in the target tenant to grant tenant-wide consent, or revise app scopes to non-admin delegated permissions.

claims.text: App registration is initiated by selecting New registration under App registrations in Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Browse to Identity > Applications > App registrations and select New registration .

claims.text: Client secrets are created under Certificates & secrets in the app registration.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Select Certificates & secrets > Client secrets > New client secret .

claims.text: Client secret lifetime is limited to a maximum of 24 months.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Client secret lifetime is limited to two years (24 months) or less.

claims.text: Redirect URIs are added on the Redirect URI configuration tab under Authentication.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: On the Redirect URI configuration tab, select Add Redirect URI .

claims.text: Redirect URIs must begin with the HTTPS scheme, except for certain localhost URIs.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Redirect URIs must begin with the scheme https , with exceptions for some localhost redirect URIs.

claims.text: Single-page application redirect URIs must be set to type spa using the application manifest editor.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Update a redirect URI : Set the redirect URI's type to spa by using the application manifest editor in the Microsoft Entra admin center.

claims.text: Some permissions like Directory.ReadWrite.All are admin-restricted and require Global Administrator consent.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Some permissions are admin-restricted, for example, writing data to an organization's directory by using Directory.ReadWrite.All .

claims.text: The authorization code flow redirects the user to the Microsoft identity platform /authorize endpoint.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: In the flow, the app redirects the user to the Microsoft identity platform /authorize endpoint.

claims.text: The offline_access permission is a standard OIDC scope requested to obtain a refresh token.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: The offline_access permission is a standard OIDC scope that's requested so that the app can get a refresh token.

claims.text: An access token is requested by sending a POST request containing the authorization code to the /token endpoint.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: The app uses the authorization code received in the previous step to request an access token by sending a POST request to the /token endpoint.

claims.text: Delegated permissions allow the application to perform operations on behalf of the signed-in user.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Delegated permissions , also referred to as scopes : The permissions exposed by Microsoft Graph and that represent the operations that the app can perform on behalf of the signed-in user.

claims.text: Application permissions allow the app to access data on its own without a signed-in user.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Application permissions : Also called app roles , allow the app to access data on its own, without a signed-in user.

claims.text: Publisher verification informs users and admins about the authenticity of the publishing organization.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Publisher verification gives app users and organization admins information about the authenticity of the developer's organization

claims.text: Publisher verification requires a valid Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account Partner One ID.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: The developer must have a Partner One ID for a valid Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account that has completed the verification process.

claims.text: Apps eligible for publisher verification must be registered using a Microsoft Entra work or school account.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: The app that's to be publisher verified must be registered by using a Microsoft Entra work or school account.

claims.text: Users cannot consent to most newly registered multitenant apps that are not publisher verified when risk-based step-up consent applies.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: users can't consent to most newly registered multitenant apps that aren't publisher verified.

claims.text: A blue verified badge appears on consent prompts once publisher verification is completed.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: When the publisher of an app has been verified, a blue verified badge appears in the Microsoft Entra consent prompt

claims.text: Microsoft does not charge developers for publisher verification.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Microsoft doesn't charge developers for publisher verification. No license is required to become a verified publisher.

claims.text: Query parameters are restricted on redirect URIs configured to sign in personal Microsoft accounts.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Query parameters are not allowed in redirect URIs for any app registration configured to sign in users with personal Microsoft accounts

claims.text: Client credentials flow requires an Application ID URI as scope rather than a traditional redirect URI.
claims.label: sourced
claims.quote: Redirect-URI is recommended but not required for client-credential flow. In order to obtain an access token, you will need to provide an Application ID URI as scope .
